messages:
raj_oncall: I'm getting paged — root cause looks like upstream auth providers timing out on token introspect endpoints (Auth0 and Okta). Users can't log in and Console access is returning 502s. Investigating now.

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT P1: Multiple auth introspect failures detected -> paging oncall: raj_oncall, maria_sre. Escalation: 5m.

deploy-bot: Alert: 502/504 spiked on /auth/introspect (eu-west & us-east). 90th latency ~8s, error rate 28% in last 5m.

maria_sre: Confirming. I can reproduce: login flows time out at introspect step. Some token verifications return 502, others return 504. Console sessions fail to initialize.

sofia_ops: Any recent deploys to auth integrations? I didn't see infra changes.

jason_prodeng: No deploys on our side to the auth lib. This looks upstream. Have we checked provider status pages?

sam_support: Tickets coming in — customers reporting "can't sign in" and "console shows an error". Support queue jumping already. Sending high-level comms to CS.

maria_sre: Checked provider status pages: Auth0 reports "degraded performance" in multiple regions (tweeted). Okta shows partial outage on token validation. Both mention increased error rates on introspect endpoints.

raj_oncall: Good. Scope: logins failing across web + API clients that do introspect calls. Existing sessions with cached tokens still ok. New token validation attempts fail. Customer impact: all customers using hosted auth, and some SSO customers.

sofia_ops: Can we circuit-break retries to reduce pressure? Our clients backoff, but the spike looks to be the external provider flapping.

maria_sre: Rolling mitigation plan: 1) Increase client-side timeout to 10s (temporary) 2) Switch introspect to regional backups where available 3) If available, use cached JWKs + local verification for signed tokens instead of introspect (only for JWT flows).

raj_oncall: For safety we should avoid changing verification semantics for auth-sensitive flows without sign-off. Can we do a limited canary: enable local JWT verification only for non-admin tenants?

jason_prodeng: We have a feature flag to prefer local signature check if token is JWT and kid present. It was intended for provider downtime. We can enable it for 20% of traffic as a canary.

sam_support: Is that safe? Will it bypass server-side revocation checks? We need to document limitations to CS.

maria_sre: Good point. Local verification won't detect revoked tokens (since introspect is authoritative). We'll only use it for login path to allow access to console, and will mark accounts as "at risk" in logs. Also will avoid applying to SSO-admin roles.

raj_oncall: Ok enable the flag to 20% across non-admin tenants. Monitor error rate and auth failures. Prepare rollback helm config ready.

sofia_ops: Deploying feature flag now: toggling rollout key auth.local_verify.canary -> 20% non-admin. Command: 

```
# feature flagging CLI
ffctl rollout set auth.local_verify.canary --percentage 20 --exclude-role admin
```

sofia_ops: Done. Rolling out to service in us-east first.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: service-auth v3.12.1 -> canary 20% (us-east). Healthcheck: auth-introspect fallback path enabled.

maria_sre: We're seeing a drop in login failures from 28% -> 18% in canary traffic. CPU/RPS stable. No new errors in logs for canary.

raj_oncall: Good. Start increasing to 50% if stable for 5m. Keep excluded admin set.

sofia_ops: Increasing to 50% now.

deploy-bot: Canary update: 50% rollout in both us-east and eu-west.

sam_support: Customers on canary path reporting successful logins. I'll update CS that partial mitigation is in place; mention risk (revocation not checked).

jason_prodeng: While we run this, can we also throttle our retry loops to reduce flood to upstream? Set retries to 1 and add jitter.

maria_sre: On it. Patching SDK config: max_retries=1, base_backoff=200ms, max_backoff=2s. Pushed to prod.

raj_oncall: Also notify security and product: local verification is temporary and reduces revocation safety.

sam_support: Drafting status update: "We are seeing degraded performance with our identity provider partners causing new sign-ins to fail. We're enabling a temporary, limited fallback to local token verification for non-admin customers — this should restore logins for affected users but does not support immediate revocation. We will revert once providers stabilize." Will send in 5m.

maria_sre: Monitoring: overall auth failures dropped to 7% after 50% rollout. Error rate on providers still high but our load against them down due to local verify fallback + lower retries.

raj_oncall: Good. Start scaling fallback to 80% for non-admins to minimize impact. Keep admin off fallback.

sofia_ops: Scaling to 80% now.

deploy-bot: Rollout: 80% complete. No critical regressions observed.

maria_sre: Observability note: add a metric tag for fallback_used=true so we can track sessions allowed via local verification. Also ensure we log token_kid and issuer for postmortem.

jason_prodeng: Adding metrics and extra log fields now. Will ship a small patch in 2m.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: Handoff scheduled in 40m. Next oncall: maria_sre -> yi_azure. Please include runbook steps in the handoff note.

raj_oncall: Preparing handoff doc: current state, mitigations, risk, customer impact, rollback steps.

sam_support: CS status update posted. Link: https://redwood.status/incident/2028-auth-external-1 (draft) — sharing with legal for compliance wording.

maria_sre: Auth0 status page: still degraded. Okta maintenance announced but not ETA. We should plan for prolonged outage. Action items: 1) Keep fallback at 80% 2) Expand to 100% for non-admin if providers don't improve in 30m 3) Consider temporary self-hosted token verification for SSO customers on request (requires support contact) 4) Prepare postmortem checklist.

raj_oncall: Agreed. If providers don't show improvement in 30m, escalate to 100% non-admin fallback. Do not enable fallback for admin or critical-ops roles.

sofia_ops: Noted. I'll prepare the rollback commands and keep the feature flag ready to disable quickly.

sam_support: We've routed urgent enterprise customers to a dedicated Slack channel and offered manual SSO re-link steps for blocked users. Logging all requests.

maria_sre: Monitoring: provider error rate unchanged. P1 checklist: impact quantification, timeline, mitigation actions, risk assessment. We should also capture which customers had admin login failures (they're still blocked).

pagerduty-bot: Handoff time approaching: 20m. Next oncall: yi_azure.

raj_oncall: Wrapping up: mitigation in place (80% local verify), retries reduced, metrics added, CS updated, legal looped in. If anyone is on-call after me, continue to watch metrics and be ready to escalate to 100% fallback at 30m if upstream remains down.

jason_prodeng: I'll coordinate a follow-up postmortem to look at longer-term options (cached introspect, revocation streaming, contract SLAs with providers).

sam_support: Will keep support triage running and escalate any admin-impact customers to engineering hotline.

maria_sre: Handoff note posted in #oncall-handoffs with steps, config snippets, and rollback commands.

raj_oncall: Handoff: @maria_sre taking over in 10m. Leaving notes in the handoff doc. Paging out. :rotating_light:

maria_sre: Acknowledged. Taking oncall. Monitoring continues.

pagerduty-bot: Incident P1 still open. Next check-in in 15m or on any regression.

sam_support: Closing loop with CS and support — will update customers if anything changes.

maria_sre: (later) Providers still degraded after handoff. I've bumped fallback to 100% for non-admins at 1801255090. Admins remain blocked; contacting account reps for enterprise customers.

raj_oncall: Thanks team. Leaving final note: we'll keep this incident open until provider restores introspect endpoints or we implement a permanent safe fallback.
